turns.t: Right, I'm here for the hand. They said to come back, but I've got to be somewhere by two, so can we crack on?
We'll be as quick as safely possible. Remind me what happened, I've only got the triage note. ~
Chopping onions. The knife slipped, cut across the palm, on the left. It bled like mad. I had it glued and strapped up yesterday at the walk-in.
Okay. Did anything else happen, did you feel your fingers go numb?
No. No numbness, fingers all move.
And has it been oozing at all, or leaking through the dressing?
No. Dry as a bone.
Have you had any fever, or felt feverish?
No. Not at all.
I've got the dressing trolley, doctor, shall I take the old one off? ~
Please, Kerry. Mr Barlow, this will be easier if we take the dressing off together, if that's all right. ~
Go on. Quickly. ~
Sorry, that'll sting a little.
Thanks. That's looking tidy. The edges are together, there's no redness around it and no pus.
So it's healing? ~
It's healing well. While we're here, I'll update your record. Are you allergic to anything? Any allergies?
None.
What medicines are you taking, if any?
Just ibuprofen, 400 mg, when it throbs. Not often.
Good. And your health background?
Type 2 diabetes, high blood pressure, and asthma, though I haven't needed the inhaler in years.
Do you want the glue left on, doctor? ~
Yes, it'll come off by itself in a week or so. Kerry, use a clean dry dressing over the top. ~
Of course. ~
Mr Barlow, any operations on this hand before?
Carpal tunnel on that wrist, in 2020. This scar here.
I see it. Thank you. It's good that the glued wound is clean. With diabetes I want to be extra careful, so keep it dry for the next five days.
Can I wash up? ~
Wear a rubber glove over a dry dressing, or let someone else do it. ~
I'll give you spare dressings to take with you. ~
Thanks. ~
Change it every day, and keep it clean.
And if it gets red, swollen, starts to ooze, or you get a temperature, come straight back or go to the urgent care centre.
Right. Will do. Can I go now? ~
You can. Mind that hand. ~
